q: Name a module in the Python standard library.

answers.l: Operating system interfaces. os.environ holds your environment.
Interpreter internals: argv, path, exit and the recursion limit.
Started life as the third-party simplejson.
Regular expressions. Compiled patterns are cached for you.
Naive versus aware datetimes: the bug that never ends.
A Mersenne Twister. Not for secrets; use secrets.
time.monotonic for durations. time.time can jump.
Lazy combinatorics, inspired by APL, Haskell and SML.
lru_cache, partial and reduce, which was demoted here from builtins in Python 3.
shell=True is how injection bugs get in.
Paths as objects. The / operator joins them.
Modeled on Java’s log4j, which is why it uses camelCase.
Originally PyUnit, after JUnit. Hence setUp and assertEqual.
Open files with newline="" or Windows will double your line breaks.
Real OS threads, limited by the GIL until free-threaded builds.
Sidesteps the GIL by using processes.
Never unpickle untrusted data. It can run arbitrary code.
High-level file operations: copy trees, remove trees, find executables.
The standard library’s HTTP client, which is why requests exists.
A full SQL database in the standard library.
Packs and unpacks C structs and binary formats.
A min-heap on a plain list.
@contextmanager turns a generator into a with-block.
Safe temporary files, without race conditions.
uuid4 for random IDs. uuid1 leaks your MAC address.
The debugger. breakpoint() drops you into it since 3.7.
Introspect live objects, signatures and frames.
Thread and process pools behind one API.
StringIO, BytesIO and the I/O stack.
Functions for every operator, like itemgetter.
python -m http.server serves the current directory.
Parsers for XML. Read the security warnings first.
Tk GUI bindings, included with Python.
The import system, written in Python.
Diffs, and get_close_matches for "did you mean" features.
Parse Python into a syntax tree.
Controls the cycle collector. Reference counting does the rest.
References that don’t keep objects alive.
Call C libraries with no compiler.
Compact arrays of one numeric type.
Signal handlers run only on the main thread.
DeprecationWarning is hidden by default outside __main__.
Encoders, decoders, and the rot_13 codec.
Names, categories and normalization for every code point.
Shell-style splitting and quoting. shlex.quote saves lives.
Opens URLs in the user’s browser.
GNU readline: line editing and history.
Which OS, which machine, which Python.
Keyed hashing. Use compare_digest to compare.
IPv4 and IPv6 addresses and networks.
Loop over lines from many files or stdin.
The Unix password database. Not your working directory.
Traces memory allocations to source lines.
"from __future__ import braces" raises SyntaxError: not a chance.
"import this" prints the Zen of Python, which is stored ROT13-encoded in its source.
"import antigravity" opens xkcd 353 in your browser.
High-level I/O multiplexing over select and friends.
Runs automatically at startup to set up sys.path.
Converts between RGB, HLS, HSV and YIQ.
Random access to source lines, used by tracebacks.
Tells whether typed code is complete yet.
Puts the terminal into raw mode.
Import modules straight from zip files.
Utilities for packages and namespace packages.

nope.numpy: Third-party. Not in the standard library.
nope.pandas: Third-party. Not in the standard library.
nope.requests: Third-party, though it feels like it should be standard.
nope.six: Third-party, and hopefully no longer needed.
nope.telnetlib: Removed in Python 3.13 by PEP 594, the "dead batteries" cleanup.
